p.t: In short
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: Check the **order status** before you answer any tracking message.
**Processing** (preparing the order) and **transit** (the trip to the customer) are two different times. Keep them apart.
Use a ready reply for each case. Pick the one that matches the order's status.
Offer a **free reship** (a new parcel at no cost) first. Offer a **full refund** when the customer asks for one or when the parcel is lost.
Promise a delivery time you can really keep, because late parcels bring complaints and refund demands.
Tell customers where their order is before they ask, because shipping from suppliers often takes **5 to 14 days**.
Hide the shipping origin on tracking and emails, so customers do not feel tricked later.
Why tracking and order status matter
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: An **order tracking system** (a way to follow where a parcel is) stops orders from disappearing.
Orders can disappear because of **supplier delays** (the company that ships the product is slow), emails lost in the inbox, or mistakes by staff.

The risk grows as **order volume** (the number of orders) grows.
The risk is highest with new suppliers whose **reliability** (how dependable they are) is not yet proven.
Tracking questions are the **most frequent** support request.
Prepare standard replies for four common cases: order not shipped yet, order shipped, shipped but not received, and shipped with an angry customer.
Most customer messages are about **legitimacy** (whether the store is real), order status, and stock (whether items are available).
Detailed product pages, an FAQ (a page of common questions and answers) and automated tracking emails remove most of these questions.
An **order tracking tool** (an app that follows parcels) can send tracking information to customers automatically after shipment.
This reduces "where is my order" **contacts** (messages sent to support).
Automatic shipment updates sent through a tracking app reduce customer inquiries about order status.
Order status check before every reply
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: **Look up** the order status in the store admin (the back office where the store is managed) and the **fulfillment system** (the system that packs and ships orders) before replying to any tracking question.
2. If the order is **not shipped yet**, send the not-shipped reply.
It says the order is being processed (being prepared to leave), a tracking email follows once it ships, and orders take about **10-20 days** after shipping.
3. If the order is shipped and the customer asks about tracking, send the shipped reply.
Include the shipping date, the **3-5 business day** delay for tracking (a business day is a working day, Monday to Friday), the **tracking link** (a web address that shows the parcel's status),
and a screenshot (a picture) of the current status.

4. If the order is shipped and the customer says they got no confirmation emails, send the **junk/spam version** (the version for this case) of the shipped reply. Ask them to check junk and spam first.
5. If the order is shipped but the customer is angry, send the angry reply with the current status.
Take responsibility for delivery and promise a **free reship** or a **full refund** if the parcel is lost in transit (on the way).

6. If the parcel is delivered and the customer wants a refund, offer a **free reship** first. Skip this only if they ask for a refund on first contact. In that case, process the refund without pushing a reship.
7. If the tracking cannot be found at all and the parcel appears lost, send the lost-order refund reply. Confirm the refund is **already started**.
Delivery times: processing and transit
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t:
Sources give different values for the same stages. Each value applies to the case listed.
Two words to know:

**Calendar days** count every day, weekends included.
**Business days** count only working days.
**Dispatch of in-stock orders from the warehouse**

Value: Within 5 business days from the order date
When it applies: Warehouse with in-stock items
**Processing before a dropshipped order ships**
Value: About 4 to 7 days

When it applies: Dropshipping store (you sell, and the supplier ships directly to the customer), order not yet shipped; the value to quote in the AI responder (an AI that writes replies) and in the not-shipped replies

**Processing example**
Value: About 3 days before shipment (Illinois to Philadelphia example)

When it applies: Single supplier case used to show processing and transit must be separated
**Physical product shipping for dropshipping**
Value: 5 to 14 days

When it applies: General shipping range for physical dropshipped products
**International transit**
Value: 10-20 days after shipping (calendar basis)

When it applies: Used in the not-shipped and shipped templates that say "after shipping"
**International transit**

Value: 10-20 business days after processing
When it applies: Used in the shipped templates that say "after processing"
**Transit to final address**

Value: 10 to 20 days from the shipping date
When it applies: Used in the not-shipped reply that cites the shipping date

Use **one basis** for transit time in every template, preferably business days, so customers do not get conflicting estimates.
Present delivery timelines as **estimates** (not promises).
Keep supplier processing time separate from **carrier transit** (the time the delivery company takes).
Do not promise a deadline that cannot be met. When processing takes about **3 days** before a shipment from Illinois to Philadelphia, a **5-business-day** deadline cannot be guaranteed.

Say that upfront.
Set expectations with the customer before they become frustrated.

Give customers a rough delivery window once a sale is made, such as **one to two weeks**. Base it on where the parcel is in the shipping process, for example after **customs** (the border check) and on its way.
Update it when possible.
Tracking numbers and tracking updates
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: **First tracking information appears**

Value: Within 24 hours of shipment, sent to the checkout email
When it applies: Store that sends tracking itself at dispatch

**First tracking information appears**
Value: Within 3-5 business days of shipping

When it applies: Standard Source C replies (the store's standard reply set), shipped and junk/spam versions
**First tracking information appears**

Value: 3 to 5 days after shipping (no business-day qualifier)
When it applies: Shipped reply variant
**Tracking escalation (passing the case to a higher level)**

Value: If no tracking after six business days, contact the support address
When it applies: Escalation rule in the in-stock template

Tracking numbers often do not update until the parcel is close to its destination.
Warn customers **not to panic** when the status stays unchanged for a while.

The tracking number does not show precise updates until the parcel is close to its destination.
State this in **every** shipped reply.
Check the status yourself on a **public tracking website** (a free site where anyone can enter a tracking number) first. Then send the customer a screenshot of the page.
Give customers the tracking number when they ask for it. **PayPal** (a payment service) and other payment providers may ask for it as proof of shipment.
Tracking tools and apps
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: **Shopify built-in shipping notifications (Shopify is the store software)**

What it does: Sends tracking numbers entered directly in Shopify to customers
Notes: Can replace AfterShip to save its monthly cost (2024)
**AfterShip (a tracking app)**
What it does: Sends automatic updates at each carrier status change (in transit to a city, arriving soon, out for delivery, delivery attempt missed)

Notes: Enter a tracking number once; prevents many support contacts; more customization than built-in notifications
**Track123 (a tracking app)**

What it does: Order tracking page app
Notes: Every store should have a tracking page
**Track123 configuration**

What it does: Updates order emails automatically and links the tracking page in the store menu
Notes: Lets customers check their order at any time

**CJ Dropshipping app (a supplier app that connects to Shopify)**
What it does: Sends an email with tracking information once a tracking number is generated

Notes: Automatic customer email at tracking generation
**Public tracking website (e.g. 17track)**

What it does: Customer enters tracking number to see package location
Notes: Used as the source for screenshots and tracking links
A **tracking page** (a page on your store that shows parcel status) serves existing customers who want to follow their parcel.
It also gives **prospects** (people who may buy) a sign that the business uses real tracking numbers. This adds **credibility** (trust) before they buy.
Confirmation emails for order, shipping and delivery can land in the **junk or spam folder**.

When a customer says they received nothing, ask them to check those folders first.
Automated emails sent by a store or its platform can land in the spam folder.
Before reporting a missing confirmation or account email, search both the main inbox and the spam folder for the sender's name. (2025)
If support emails seem missing, check the spam folder first. Replies may land there.
If you are in the mentor program, also post in the member **Slack channel** (a group chat room) to get attention faster.

The standard response to a delivery complaint takes **responsibility** for the shipment.
The same response apologizes for the inconvenience. Then it offers a **free reship or full refund** if the package is lost in transit.
For a package lost in transit, offer the customer **either a free replacement shipment or a full refund**.
Make this offer explicitly in the reply to an impatient customer whose order is still moving.
Guarantees and refund policy
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: State a **guarantee** (a promise) covering every package to customers.

If a parcel is lost in transit, the customer may choose a **full refund or a free reship**.
The store can add a **store credit** (money to spend in the store) on top of the reship.

The default refund policy (the standard rule) is that a customer can get either a **free reship or a full refund**.
The preferred first offer is a **free reship**.
If the customer asks for a refund on first contact, give the refund without pushing a reship.
For lost shipments, send the tracking information that shows the item was lost.

Then keep the customer updated on **replacements**, when they ship and when they arrive.
Most customers only panic when they are not kept informed.
If the fulfillment platform can no longer track an order and the package is considered lost, **issue a full refund**.

Tell the customer the refund has **already been initiated** (started).
Do not wait for the customer to ask for a replacement before refunding.
Write a reply for a lost order where the tracking has gone missing, using this structure: explain that the package appears to have disappeared from the system

and that the reason the tracking cannot be found is unknown; state that a full refund is being provided and has already been initiated, with an email notification to follow; apologize for the inconvenience
and thank the customer for their patience; sign off as the store customer support representative.

The process has already begun, and you should receive an email about it. I'm sorry for any trouble this has caused, and thank you for your patience while we resolve this.
Thanks, [AGENT NAME] [STORE NAME] Customer Support Representative

It has already been initiated, and you should receive an email notifying you of this. We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your patience during this issue.
Thanks, [agent name], [store name] Customer Support Representative
Late delivery and delay responses
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: When a customer complains about a late delivery, first find the **cause** before choosing a remedy (a fix).

Possible causes are outdated product page delivery times, slow order submission, or a supplier that took longer than usual.
Each cause has a different fix.
If a supplier never ships a paid order and the customer becomes upset, a partial refund such as **5%** combined with a firm delivery date can settle the situation.

The exact remedy depends on what went wrong.
For delivery questions, promise only what the supplier and carrier can deliver.
Contact the store team when a customer needs a quote instead of guessing a price.
Hi [Customer name], thank you for your message and for your patience. Your order is on its way, but delivery is taking a little longer than usual.
We are sorry for the delay and will keep you updated until it arrives. [Store name] Customer Support

Use a reply to customers who ask why an order takes so long, adjusted to your own situation: I apologize for this. Due to shipping, customs or Covid we will do our best to get your order to you on time.
In the meantime, since you are patiently waiting, here is a discount code for your next purchase: [CODE].
Hi [CUSTOMER NAME], thank you for your patience, and I am sorry your order is taking longer than expected.
It is not something you did; the delay comes from [shipping times / customs / Covid-19 delays], and we are doing our best to get your order to you on time.
While you wait, here is a [DISCOUNT %] discount code for your next purchase: [CODE]. If you have any questions, reply to this email at any time and I will keep you updated on your order.
Best regards, [YOUR NAME]
Delivery promises and Christmas
p.s: Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

p.t: Setting delivery times that are too short is **over-promising**.

(Over-promising means promising more than you can deliver.)
Short delivery times may raise **conversion**. (Conversion means the share of visitors who buy.)
But customers who get their parcel later than promised lead to complaints and chargebacks. (A chargeback is when a customer asks their bank to take the money back.)
Set the estimate to what the **fulfillment center** can reliably meet. (A fulfillment center is the warehouse that packs and ships your orders.)

Improve the estimate as your setup matures.
A prompt is an instruction you give to an AI writing tool. Copy this one as it is:
Write a Christmas guarantee message for a shipment expected before the holiday: greet the customer by name; say the order is on its way and is promised to arrive before Christmas; state that
if delivery takes longer, a full refund will be given; sign off with the agent name and store customer support representative title.
A template is ready-made text with blanks. Replace each blank in square brackets with your own details: [NAME], [AGENT NAME], and [STORE NAME].
Hi [NAME], Your order is currently on its way to you, and we promise it will arrive before Christmas. If it takes any longer than that, we will happily provide a full refund.
Warm regards, [AGENT NAME] [STORE NAME] Customer Support Representative
Some customers do not know their parcel ships from China. (Origin means where the parcel comes from.)

If they find out later, they become more anxious.
So **hide the origin** on tracking and emails.
This protects trust after the purchase. (Trust means the customer feels safe buying from you.)
For dropshipping with physical products, shipping can take **5 to 14 days**. (Dropshipping means your supplier ships the product straight to the customer.

Physical products are goods you can hold, not digital files.)
So customers will often ask where their order is.
Tracking is the code and page that show where the parcel is.
Plan **customer service** for these tracking questions from the start. (Customer service means your team that answers customer questions.)
